comment: audit-bundle.mjs's allowlist (20261005-portable-app-download): `files` are the patterns every file of the packaged .app must match (the file list), `allow` the build-shaped paths that may appear, each with its reason. This machine's own paths (home, checkout, ~/.bun, ~/.t3, the temporary folder, every --forbid) are never allowed.

allow.reason: Not a path: the template literal `/Users/${user}` of terminal-links.ts (a terminal link's home-folder form), which the Hermes string table stores beside the next literal, /api/auth/session.

package-app.mjs's fixed export folder, the same on every machine (no user, checkout or home path): exact2's ibex2 build.rs and js/build.rs give hermesc absolute source paths, and Hermes keeps them as the bytecode's file names (EXACT2-GAPS X50). Rust paths are remapped and Swift's are stripped; these two cannot be from the app.

GitHub Actions' macOS runner home: T3 Code's release CI (the executable's bin.mjs path) and the prebuilt binaries the release bundles (ripgrep, fff, keyring, ffi-rs, node-pty, Cursor's sandbox, the resource monitor). The release's own bytes, unpacked unchanged and equal to runtime-manifest.json and the pin's SHA-256.
Node.js's release build machine: source paths compiled into the Node single executable the T3 release is built on (V8, Temporal, the inspector protocol). The release's own bytes.
The temporary folder Cursor's SDK built its tree-sitter prebuilds in, on its build machine (not this one: this machine's temporary folder is a machine path). The release's own bytes.

Not a path of any machine: string literals in the release's JavaScript and executable (the temporary-folder and home-folder prefixes its path checks and display use, Homebrew's and Bun's default folders where the server looks for provider CLIs).
